source_metadata.title: Trends in Invasive Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Infections

sections: Results: Characteristics of Invasive MRSA Isolates
Results: Invasive MRSA Infection Incidence and Trends
omissions: Reference entries were excluded from atomization and used only to build the separate task queue.
Acknowledgments were not atomized because they contain contributor credits rather than independently reviewable study assertions.

consistency_findings: The abstract reports the CA yearly-change confidence interval upper bound as 18.2%, while the Results/Figure 2 report 18.3%; atoms use the full Results/Figure 2 value and preserve the discrepancy here.
Table 1 total N=876 includes early-onset and unclassified cases; the epidemiologic-category counts sum to 857. These populations were kept distinct.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema requires an exposure descriptor for quantitative_result and subgroup_result atoms even for descriptive surveillance estimates without a causal exposure; cohort/time/category descriptors were used conservatively as observational exposures.

The schema has no dedicated fields for medians with interquartile ranges or for national-estimate count confidence intervals, so those details are preserved in canonical_statement/original_result_text and arm observations.
extraction_limitations: No claim was created from reference-list content itself.
The study contains no supplementary appendix in the retrieved PDF.
The submitted isolate sample was a convenience sample, and this limitation is represented as a separate atom.
